text: Git branching is a powerful tool for managing changes in software projects. When you create a feature branch, you work on a new idea or fix without affecting the main codebase. This keeps your main branch stable and ready for release at any time. After finishing your work, you request a pull request, which lets teammates review your changes before they are merged. Merging combines your branch back into the main branch, integrating your updates. This workflow encourages collaboration and reduces errors, as everyone sees and approves changes before they become part of the project. It’s a simple yet effective way to keep your code organized and safe.
